t.1.169.1: Then Adṛśyantī, dwelling in the hermitage, gave birth to a son, O king, the perpetuator of Śakti's line, like a second Śakti.
t.1.169.2: O best of the Bharatas, that blessed bull among sages himself performed for his grandson the rites beginning with the birth ceremony.
t.1.169.4: That righteous-souled one then regarded Vasiṣṭha as his father, and from his very birth he conducted himself toward him as toward a father.
t.1.169.3: Because Vasiṣṭha, who was on the point of death, was then made to remain in life by him while he was still in the womb, he is therefore known in the world as Parāśara.
t.1.169.5: O son of Kuntī, scorcher of foes, in the presence of his mother Adṛśyantī, he addressed the brahmin seer Vasiṣṭha as “Father.”
t.1.169.6: Hearing that sweet word of his, “Father,” so full of meaning, Adṛśyantī, her eyes brimming with tears, spoke to him.
t.1.169.7: Do not keep saying 'Father, father, father,' my child; this great sage is not your father. Your father, child, was devoured by a Rākṣasa deep in the forest.
t.1.169.9: Thus addressed, that truthful one, best of seers, high-minded and stricken with grief, set his mind upon the destruction of all the worlds.
t.1.169.8: The one whom you think of as “Father,” O sinless one, is not your father; this noble one is the father of your great-souled father.
t.1.169.10: Vasiṣṭha, of great austerity, restrained that great-souled one whose mind was thus resolved; hear the reason by which he did so.
t.1.169.11: Vasiṣṭha said: There was on earth a king renowned as Kṛtavīrya, a bull among rulers, who in this world was the patron of sacrifice of the Bhṛgus, those knowers of the Veda.
t.1.169.13: Then, when that tiger among kings had gone to heaven, at some time there arose for those born of his lineage a need for wealth.
t.1.169.12: At the end of the Soma sacrifice, my dear, that lord of the people gratified those who are first to partake of the offerings with abundant grain and wealth.
t.1.169.14: Those kings, all of them, having learned of the wealth of the Bhṛgus, came begging to those best of the Bhārgavas, my dear son.
t.1.169.15: Some of the Bhṛgus buried their inexhaustible wealth in the ground, while others, knowing the danger from the Kṣatriya, gave it away to the twice-born.
t.1.169.16: But some of the Bhṛgus then gave wealth to those kṣatriyas as they desired, my dear son, foreseeing another cause.
t.1.169.17: Then, dear son, a certain kṣatriya, digging the surface of the earth by chance, found wealth in the house of the Bhṛgus; all the bulls among kṣatriyas, gathered together, saw that wealth.
t.1.169.18: Then, in their anger, disregarding those Bhṛgus who had come seeking refuge, those great archers slew them all with sharpened arrows, and they roamed the earth cutting them down even down to the unborn in the womb.
t.1.169.19: Then, as the Bhṛgus were being thus exterminated, the wives of the Bhṛgus, out of fear, took refuge at that time in the mountain Himavant, my dear.
t.1.169.20: One of those women, a lovely-thighed one, out of fear held in one thigh a fiery embryo for the increase of her husband's lineage. They saw that brahmin woman blazing with her own splendor.
t.1.169.22: Then those bulls among kṣatriyas, their purposes thwarted and stricken with fear, went for refuge to that blameless brahmin woman for the sake of their sight.
t.1.169.23: And those Kṣatriyas, bewildered, bereft of their sight and stricken with grief, like fires whose flames have died down, spoke to that illustrious lady.
t.1.169.21: Then that embryo split open the brahmin woman's thigh and came forth, robbing the kṣatriyas of their sight like the sun at midday. Then, deprived of their sight, they wandered about among the mountain fastnesses.
t.1.169.24: By the grace of the blessed lady, may the warrior class go forth with its sight restored; and, having desisted from our evil deed, let us depart together.
t.1.169.25: Together with your son, you ought to show favor to all of us; by granting the king his sight once more, you ought to save us.
